title: Miso-Glazed Salmon
summary: Salmon fillets brushed with a sweet miso and mirin glaze and broiled until caramelized at the edges. Ten minutes of cooking for a weeknight that feels special.

creator.bio: Sample creator. Simple Japanese home meals: rice bowls, noodles and quick glazes.

steps.instruction: Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches below it. Line a baking tray with foil and brush it with the oil.
Mix the miso, mirin, sugar and soy sauce in a small bowl until smooth.
success_cues: Glaze is smooth and spreadable, like thick yogurt

steps.instruction: Pat the salmon dry and set it skin side down on the tray. Spread the glaze over the tops and sides.
success_cues: Each fillet is covered in an even thin layer of glaze
warnings: Raw fish: wash hands and tools after handling. Check the thickest part reaches 145°F (63°C) with a thermometer rather than relying on looks.

steps.instruction: Broil 7 to 10 minutes, depending on thickness, watching closely after 5 minutes.
success_cues: Glaze is bubbling and browned at the edges
A thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F (63°C)
warnings: Sugar in the glaze can scorch fast under the broiler; move the tray lower if it darkens before the fish is done.
Raw fish: wash hands and tools after handling. Check the thickest part reaches 145°F (63°C) with a thermometer rather than relying on looks.
steps.creator_note: A little char on the edges is the best part. Black is too far.

steps.instruction: Rest 2 minutes, then serve over rice with scallion if using.
success_cues: Flesh flakes into large moist pieces
warnings: The tray is very hot; use oven mitts.

creator_notes: Leftover salmon flaked over rice with a little soy sauce makes a great lunch.
dietary_warnings: Contains fish, soy and wheat (miso, soy sauce).
